mappings.note: Same medium-over-xhigh result for Opus on one run; video says ~3 points vs article 1.5 (28 vs 25); single run, so noise caveat applies.
Narrows the family: for the OpenAI models medium is cheaper but worse, so medium-by-default does not hold across model families.
Dex's own live caveat that the split may be the shape of this benchmark; consistent with treating single-run gaps as noise.
For OpenAI models more effort buys more strict passes at higher cost, with an upward cost-vs-success trend, against the claim that spend is a weak predictor.
Fable xhigh very expensive and not impressive on strict passes; Dex repositions it as a spec double-checker.
Dex uses Fable as a spec/verifier role rather than a coder; same cheap-writer, smart-checker routing.
Strict pass definition: current plus all inherited regression tests; adds that one regression caps all later strict scores.
Benchmark description: ~196 checkpoints, 3-8 per challenge, each inheriting prior code (30 vs 36 problems inconsistency).
Even the best run ends with failing final tests (Astra 3 of 36 clean), so checkpoint success is not a working final program.
Lights-off factory feeding features accumulates slop and compounds, so correctness odds fall over time.
Nobody has worked out how to RL for maintainability, so models are good at coding but not maintainability.
Token cost and agent time matter less than long-term maintainability; users would pay about twice the tokens for cleaner code.
Scratch, test and verifier leftovers count against quality; article gives the filter result (only Opus Medium _work folder affected).
Adds the detector composition: ~150 custom AST slop linters plus 50-60 standard metrics (~212), with function-level hits marking whole functions as slop.
Opus xhigh lowest slop coverage (77.75% vs 94.25%) despite fewer strict passes; quality metric did not predict pass rate.
Slop linters are partly stale (many from March), so detectors need regular refresh and may miss new patterns.
Fable had lowest mean complexity and nearly most functions, but small functions do not mean not slop; single metric can be gamed.
Each model ran in its own default harness, so model and harness effects are mixed in the comparison.
Complexity/quality metrics as back pressure; relayed from co-host's BAML experiment, no Dex-run numbers.
Dex plans to test plain 'build it' vs feedback battery or quality target; confirms the effect is still untested.
With a benchmark plus quality metrics, many skill/linter variants can be measured by git diff, so skills are tested not assumed.
Undeveloped aside that tests are pointless for fast zero-to-one throwaway work; no family makes this claim.
Models refactor well when told but do not volunteer centralising or abstraction redefinition, so refactor steps must be asked for.
